quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

36 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: You are driving in the far right lane of a four-lane freeway. You notice thick broken white lines on the left side of your lane. You are driving in:

options.text: The carpool lane and must merge into the next lane.
A special lane for slow-moving vehicles.
An exit lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: An exit lane.
questions.explanation: Thick broken white lines on a freeway mark the end of a lane. Be prepared to exit the freeway or for your lane to end.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should return to your original lane when:

options.text: You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
You have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.
You are 50 feet in front of the passed vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Move back into your original lane only when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror. This gives you enough safe space.

questions.question: You must show proof of insurance to law enforcement:

options.text: Only if you are involved in a collision.
If you are involved in a collision or stopped for a citation.
Only if you are stopped and cited.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are involved in a collision or stopped for a citation.
questions.explanation: You must have proof of insurance with you whenever you drive. Show it to an officer after a traffic stop or collision.

questions.question: A sign with this shape means:

options.text: No passing zone.
Right turn permitted on red.
Yield right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: A pennant-shaped sign marks where a no passing zone begins.

questions.question: You are approaching a green traffic light but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partially enter the intersection to establish your right-of-way.
Don't enter the intersection until you can get completely across.
Continue into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't enter the intersection until you can get completely across.
questions.explanation: Even if your light is green, do not enter the intersection unless you can drive completely through it before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you should:

options.text: Watch for traffic merging from the right.
Merge right.
Turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for traffic merging from the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that traffic may merge into your lane from the right.

questions.question: While driving, you should look 10 to 15 seconds ahead of you:

options.text: And focus on the middle of the road.
Because it is a legal requirement.
To see potential hazards early.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see potential hazards early.
questions.explanation: Scan the road 10 to 15 seconds ahead so you can spot hazards early and avoid last-minute moves.

questions.question: When should drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if the pedestrians first wave to the driver.
Only if the pedestrians are not texting while walking.
At all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a crosswalk to let pedestrians cross. You may only proceed if your lane is clear.

questions.question: To pass on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Judge the distance to any oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judge the distance to any oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: Oncoming vehicles do not always seem as fast as they really are. Make sure you can safely change lanes before passing. If you are unsure about an oncoming vehicle's speed, wait until it passes.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, you should:

options.text: Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.
Use your high beam headlights until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.
Use your high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when following another vehicle. Use high beams only in rural areas when no other cars are nearby.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Use your high beam headlights.
Use your parking lights.
Use your low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams will reflect back at you and make it harder to see.

questions.question: If you pass a school bus that is stopped with its red lights flashing, you will:

options.text: Be fined up to $1,000.
Be fined up to $100.
Face no legal consequences.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be fined up to $1,000.
questions.explanation: You must stop completely when you see a school bus with red lights flashing. Failing to stop can result in license suspension and a fine of up to $1,000.

questions.question: What message will be found on a red octagon-shaped sign?

options.text: Do not enter.
One-way.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign always means "stop." You must come to a complete stop.

questions.question: When stopped at a red traffic light with a green arrow, you may proceed in the direction of the arrow if you:

options.text: First come to a complete stop.
Wait until the light changes.
Are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: You may proceed in the direction of a green arrow if you are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear. Yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

questions.question: You enter a designated turn lane to make a left turn at an upcoming intersection. There is oncoming traffic. You should:

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal before you arrive at the intersection.
Turn your front wheels to the left to be prepared to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you arrive at the intersection.
questions.explanation: Begin signaling about 100 feet before your turn. Keep your front wheels straight ahead until it is safe to turn. This protects you if another vehicle hits you from behind.

questions.question: When you see this black and yellow sign, it means:

options.text: The road to the right is for one-way traffic only.
There is a detour to the right due to road construction.
The road ahead changes direction at an extreme angle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead changes direction at an extreme angle.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you to slow down because the road is about to change direction sharply.

questions.question: You hit a parked vehicle and can't find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked vehicle, you must leave a note with your name, phone number, and address attached to the vehicle.

questions.question: Roads with double solid yellow lines down the center indicate that passing is:

options.text: Allowed from both directions.
Allowed only from your direction of travel.
Not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means traffic is moving in opposite directions and passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: A pedestrian is crossing illegally in the middle of the street instead of at a crosswalk. You:

options.text: Must stop for them.
Do not have to stop for them.
Should honk your horn at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop for them.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians. Even if they are crossing illegally, you must still stop for them.

questions.question: You are parked and waiting a long time with your turn signal on to enter traffic. Traffic is heavy. You should:

options.text: Continue waiting and yield to the traffic.
Slowly inch your vehicle into the traffic.
Drive on the shoulder until a gap appears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue waiting and yield to the traffic.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a parked position, you must yield to all moving traffic.

questions.question: A truck's blind spots are located:

options.text: Directly behind the truck.
On the left side of the cab.
On the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.
questions.explanation: Trucks have large blind spots on both sides and behind. If you cannot see the truck driver's face in their mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: In heavy fog, you should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Turn on your high beam lights.
Turn on your low beam lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam lights.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off moisture and create glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: Extra space in front of a large truck is needed for:

options.text: Other drivers to merge.
The truck to stop.
Other drivers to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck to stop.
questions.explanation: Trucks need more space to stop than cars at the same speed. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not assume the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you use your signal.
Assume the other driver will maintain the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that other drivers will give you space or the right-of-way, even if you signal.

questions.question: With a Class C driver license, a person may drive:

options.text: A three-axle vehicle weighing less than 6,000 pounds.
Any three-axle vehicle, no matter the weight.
A vehicle pulling two trailers.

questions.correctAnswerText: A three-axle vehicle weighing less than 6,000 pounds.
questions.explanation: A Class C license allows you to drive a three-axle vehicle only if it weighs 6,000 pounds or less.

questions.question: Temporary signs in construction and work zones have:

options.text: A red background with green writing.
An orange background with black writing.
A yellow background with blue writing.

questions.correctAnswerText: An orange background with black writing.
questions.explanation: All temporary work zone signs have orange backgrounds with black writing or symbols.

questions.question: As your speed increases, it is important to:

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Look far ahead of your vehicle.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Your stopping distance increases with speed. At higher speeds, you need to see hazards far ahead to react safely.

questions.question: It is illegal to park your vehicle:

options.text: In an unmarked crosswalk.
Within three feet of a private driveway.
In a bicycle lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In an unmarked crosswalk.
questions.explanation: You cannot park in a marked or unmarked crosswalk. You may park in a bicycle lane if there is no "No parking" sign and your vehicle does not block cyclists.

questions.question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal means:

options.text: Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal your turn.
Prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turn is ending. You must prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: Higher speeds increase the chance of a fatal crash.
As speed increases, you should increase your following distance.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds greatly increase the risk of a fatal crash. Higher speeds also mean you need more distance to stop, so increase your following distance as you speed up.

questions.question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you must:

options.text: Slow down because a lane is ending.
Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and keep your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: In work zones, signs warn of workers, slow equipment, and closed lanes. You should reduce your speed and be prepared to slow down or stop.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No U-turn.
No left turn.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means right turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: On freezing, wet days, where is ice most likely to hide?

options.text: Near the tops of hills.
On bridges and overpasses.
On asphalt roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: On bridges and overpasses.
questions.explanation: Bridges and overpasses freeze before regular road surfaces. They often hide dangerous ice patches.

questions.question: When parking parallel to the curb on a level street:

options.text: Your front wheels must point toward the street.
Your wheels must be within 18 inches of the curb.
One rear wheel must touch the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your wheels must be within 18 inches of the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking along the curb on a level street, all wheels must be parallel to the curb and within 18 inches of it.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect your driving ability?

options.text: Three
Two
One

questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Even one drink affects your ability to drive safely. Do not drive after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road. To prevent it in wet weather, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to maintain constant speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is caused by driving too fast on wet pavement. Slow down on wet roads to prevent hydroplaning.
